set.st: Night operator Eugene McNally was convicted of taking about $9,000 from the depot safe at Abbotsford on 18 May 1891: $8,000 sent by the Seymour Bank, Chippewa Falls, to the State Bank of Phillips, about $1,000 more and two jewelry packages (Northern Pacific Express). His footprints were found under the depot the next morning, "very likely seeking a safe hiding place", and he was in the woods that morning walking to Colby. He got 5 years at Waupun, and "the money has never been found". In June 1892 a rumor said it had been found buried near Abbotsford, with a local family "very flush with money". The pin marks the railroad junction area where the depot likely stood, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Railroad junction area (depot inferred from track layout); story pin.
pinev: Junction-level: no Abbotsford Sanborn at LoC; the USGS topo puts the Wisconsin Central junction, where the depot would have stood, W of City Hall where the Medford branch leaves the main line (about 500 m).

cr-lemuel-hill-hoard-1906.t: He died intestate in Oct 1906 and the estate closed within about nine months; no later report of more money found.
src: Winona Daily News 1906-10-25 p9, 1907-07-23 p2 (probate notices)
